is: every sound a world can play by name, moved from the game 2099's sound catalogue (game/sound/catalogue/sound_catalogue.gd, 2026-10-09): the file it plays (a library reference, tools/library/library_files.py; a list when it has several takes, one played at random), its bus (which part of the mix it goes through: ambience, effects, felt, suit, room), whether it loops, whether it is a ground thud (felt through boots or hands, so heard even in vacuum), how loud it plays in dB, and how far a placed sound carries in metres (0: as far as it carries). data/sound/sounds.json lays each of its entries over the one here, field by field. Quiet by default: the warning tone is the loudest thing, at warning_db. Retired on 2026-10-21 (owner: every old library sound withdrawn, remade fresh): each sound's file and level went with the old sounds; how it plays (bus, loop, ground thud, reach) stays

radio_click_in.note: The owner's call: the click in and the click out are the same click.

warning_tone.note: Warnings, in the helmet. The warning tone is the loudest thing in the game.

drone_thrust_burst.note: Loops while the burn stays open: as a one-shot it ran out after five seconds of thrust.

rocket_hull_roar.note: The launch from inside the capsule, laid over the recording: the roar and crackle it lacks (the owner's playtest, 2026-10-04). A real Shuttle lift-off, ignition through the first seconds of the climb, low-passed twice at 1.1 kHz as the hull would muffle it and faded in over 2.5 s so it builds with the burn (2026-10-05; it replaced a roar made from noise).

rocket_landing_rumble.note: The steady middle of the take, its end joined into its start: the whole take swelled and died away every 14 seconds, so a long descent went quiet before the rocket was down.

rocket_touchdown.note: The loudest thing after a warning, and still well under the warning tone.

landing_thud.note: The walker coming down off a real fall: the same thud, far softer than a drone's or a rocket's. At the drone's level every hop landed with a big bass boom (first playthrough, 2026-10-01).
